newsitem.title: KUWAIT: British minister to discuss arms deals in Kuwait.
newsitem.headline: British minister to discuss arms deals in Kuwait.

text.p: British Foreign Office Minister Derek Fatchett will visit Kuwait on Monday to discuss pending arms deals and underline London's support for the security of Gulf Arab states.
Fatchett "will talk about defence supply issues which are a very important part of the relationship," said a Western source.

He is expected to discuss obstacles facing an order for British Aerospace Plc Sea Skua missiles and express unease at reports that a Kuwaiti military committee had recommended a Chinese 155mm gun over Western offers.

"A decision at the highest level has not yet been made on the guns but Britain would like to see its AS90 given a fair run, especially as the system did very well in desert trials here last year," said a Western diplomat.

Kuwait needed up to three battalions of self- propelled guns which experts said could be worth $600 million depending on specification and training. They said Kuwait's long-term total requirement was for up to five battalions.

The United States has already privately expressed its view to Kuwait during a visit this month by U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen who publicly hinted that the Chinese gun could prove to be incompatible with Kuwait's mainly Western arms.

Washington, which led the 1991 Gulf War alliance, is offering its M109 A6 Paladin which is deployed in the desert with U.S. ground forces. The South African LIW 155mm G6, the only offer for a wheeled system, seems to have been dropped from the competition, industry sources said.

There has been no official announcement but industry sources earlier told Reuters a military committee had picked China to equip a Kuwait Land Forces battalion with 18 tracked howitzers with an option for a second battalion.
Fatchett, who arrived in Oman on Sunday and is also due to visit the United Arab Emirates, is expected to tackle the Sea Skua deal -- the focus of much debate in parliament.
"Britain was told more than a year ago that Kuwait would buy Sea Skuas but it has become a politicial issue and nothing happened," said a Western diplomat.
The total package could be worth up to $150 million. The surface-to-surface Skua missiles will arm eight fast patrol boats ordered from France in 1995 in a deal worth $500 million.
